scene_summary: A small office with a table, two swivel chairs, a low cubby shelf beneath a blind, a floor lamp, a door, and a foreground plant.
overall_evidence: The principal objects and their broad arrangement are recognizable, including the shelf under the blind, lamp on the left, door on the right, and two chairs between the table and back wall. The reconstruction differs substantially in viewpoint and framing, floor and door materials, door appearance, and the visible arrangement and proportions of furniture and plant.

main_defects.description: The viewpoint is wider and more frontal, showing the whole table and more of the back wall, while the reference has a steeper downward view and crops the table and foreground plant much more strongly.
main_defects.evidence: The reference table extends beyond the lower image edge and the door occupies much of the right wall height; the reconstruction table is entirely visible and the door is smaller in frame.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent differences in object size and placement may result from viewpoint rather than scene geometry.

main_defects.description: The distinctive mottled brown wood floor and dark door are replaced by a much paler, nearly uniform tiled floor and a light gray door; the table is also noticeably lighter.
main_defects.evidence: Brown variegated flooring and a charcoal door dominate the reference, whereas the reconstruction uses pale gray flooring and door surfaces.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and exposure may contribute to color differences, but do not explain the missing floor grain.

main_defects.description: The chairs read as a more closely aligned pair facing the table in the reconstruction; in the reference the nearer chair is more prominently turned sideways and the chairs are more separated in the image.
main_defects.evidence: The reference foreground chair presents a broad side profile, while both reconstruction chairs show similar back and seat profiles.
main_defects.uncertainty: The change in camera angle accounts for an unknown portion of the apparent orientation and spacing difference.

main_defects.description: The plant foliage is much more dominant in the reconstruction, obscuring a substantial part of the door and lower right room; the door also appears smaller relative to the shelf and wall.
main_defects.evidence: The reference door is fully visible above the plant, while reconstructed foliage overlaps its lower section and fills much of the right foreground.
main_defects.uncertainty: Foreground placement and camera perspective could explain much of the apparent size difference.

main_defects.description: The door panels project as simple raised rectangles instead of the reference's dark recessed-looking outlined panels, and the blind is a thin flat rectangle rather than the deeper light-wood framed inset.
main_defects.evidence: The reconstruction has visibly raised gray door blocks and dark corner marks on the blind, unlike the reference panel outlines and substantial wood trim.
main_defects.uncertainty: The reference door panel depth is inferred only from shading and outlines; its exact construction is not observable.

strengths: The main office objects are present and broadly arranged in the same left-to-right order.
The two chairs have recognizable molded seats and wheeled pedestal bases.
The shelf has multiple open cubbies, the blind has horizontal slats, and the lamp has a slender stem and pale shade.
The plant has similarly dense, narrow spiky foliage.
uncertainty: This is a single-view visual comparison, not a verified scene or human rating. Camera, perspective, cropping, and lighting can make object proportions and orientations appear different; hidden geometry and support cannot be assessed reliably.
